description_full: Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation, a professional services company, provides consulting and technology, and outsourcing services in North America, Europe, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Financial Services; Health Sciences; Products and Resources; and Communications, Media and Technology. It provides services, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology services and solutions, consulting, application development, systems integration, quality engineering and assurance, engineering research and development, application maintenance, infrastructure, security, and business process services and automation. It also offers AI-led automation, which includes advisory, and process and IT automation solutions designed to simplify and accelerate automation adoption; business process outsourcing services, which help deliver business outcomes including revenue growth, increased customer and employee satisfaction, and cost savings; and Cognizant Moment, a digital experience service that uses AI to reimagine customer experiences and engineer strategies aimed at driving growth. It develops, licenses, implements, and supports proprietary and third-party software products and platforms; and develops industry-specific products and services. It offers solution to healthcare providers and payers, life sciences companies, banking, capital markets, payments and insurance companies, manufacturers, automakers, retailers, consumer goods, travel and hospitality, communications, media and entertainment, education, information services, and technology companies; and businesses providing logistic, energy, and utility services. It has a strategic partnership with Uniphore Technologies Inc. for the development of AI solutions that combine small language models and AI agents. It holds a strategic partnership with Travelport to build intelligent travel retail for the AI era. The company was incorporated in 1988 and is headquartered in Teaneck, New Jersey.

financial_summary: Cognizant Technology Solutions  is a large-cap technology business with a $28.2B market cap on $21.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 9% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $2.6B in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 92× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 7.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 9pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.69x).
It accounts for 0.5% of sector revenue and 0.3% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-5.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 15% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 8% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 28% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 44% and a beta of 0.93, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $364.3M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 42% in the 2020 crash, 44% in the 2022 bear market and 60% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 72% below its DCF fair value of $223, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 58%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $158 to $322 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 11.5 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 7.1 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 10.9 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 23% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 9.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 11.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 25 covering analysts target $69.78 on average, 11% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 19% clears the cost of capital of 9.2% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.49).
It converts 12% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.29x.
ROE of 15% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
It spends 0.9% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.3B (5% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 2.8% over 3 years, 4.9% over 5 years and 5.4% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -2.2% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.06 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 30% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 12%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (1.4% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 16, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 7.1% a year to shareholders (4.9% in buybacks and 2.1% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.1% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 359,900 employees, each generates about $59K of revenue, 0.2x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 12.3% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $7K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $5.7M (97x revenue per employee).
